title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
prompt:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, remove the `n`th node from the end of the list and return the head of the resulting list.

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,2,3,4,5]` represents `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, remove the target node by manipulating `next` pointers, then convert back to an array to return.

examples.explanation: The 2nd node from the end is 4, so it is removed.

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is sz
hints: Try to solve it in a single pass instead of first counting the list length.
Use two pointers separated by a gap of n nodes: advance a 'fast' pointer n steps ahead first, then move both pointers together until fast reaches the end.
Use a dummy node before the head so that removing the head itself (when n equals the list length) doesn't need special-casing.

solution.approach: Use a dummy node pointing to head so removals at the very front don't need special handling. Advance a fast pointer n+1 steps from dummy, then move a slow pointer (starting at dummy) and fast together until fast reaches the end (null). At that point slow sits just before the node to remove, so slow.next = slow.next.next skips over it. Return dummy.next.
